pages.text: "Today I'll tie the sack!" Big sister Dodo stood by a flour sack with her chin up. Flour drifted inside the mill; snow fell heavily outside. Mom held the sack open.
Little brother Mumu waddled over and saw her ribbon. "Dodo, flour on your ribbon." His floury wings rubbed it. The blue ribbon grew whiter and whiter.
"Don't touch my ribbon!" Dodo shouted and stamped. Flour puffed up, Mumu flinched backward, and startled Mom dropped the sack.
Mom sat beside Dodo. "Your chest suddenly felt hot, right?" "I know! I'm not angry!" Dodo sniffled and shook her head. "That is anger. It isn't bad. It's a guest stopping by for a moment."
"How do I send that guest away?" Dodo asked. Mom lifted her floury wing. "In through the nose, out through the mouth! A big breath to blow flour away. Angry? Blow the flour away!"

"Now, try blowing the flour away," Mom said behind her. Dodo breathed in through her nose, then blew toward her wing. Flour scattered. Her hot cheeks cooled. She grinned. "Angry? Blow the flour away!"
Dodo stood before Mumu with both wings down. "Sorry I shouted. My chest suddenly got hot. Now I blew it all away." Just then, one flick of her tail.
"It's okay, Dodo!" Mumu hopped into her wings. Then he gently preened flour off her ribbon with his beak. The blue ribbon turned blue again.

When the anger guest came, Dodo did this. "One, stop! Two, in through the nose, out through the mouth! Three, say with words, 'I'm upset!'" Even when Mumu spilled flour, Dodo breathed out. "It's okay. We can dust it off!"

Mom wrapped a wing around Dodo's back from behind. "You really are a big sister, sending anger away well!" Even anger slips away with a big breath. Tying the sack tightly, Dodo called, "Angry? Blow the flour away!"
